title: The 2025 AI Engineering Report — Barr Yaron, Amplify
talk_summary: This is a survey-results talk from a VC summarizing the 2025 State of AI Engineering survey (500 respondents), covering model usage, RAG/fine-tuning, prompt management, agents, observability, and evals. It contains almost no implementation detail or mechanisms — mostly bar charts and adoption statistics — so only a few weak signals are actionable.

takeaways.technique: Treat evaluation as the top pain point and invest in offline eval + human review
takeaways.what_they_do: Survey respondents rank evaluation as the #1 most painful thing in AI engineering; monitoring mixes standard observability (~60%), offline eval (>50%), and human review as the most popular quality method.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the number one most painful thing about AI engineering today? And evaluation topped that list
takeaways.numbers: ~60% standard observability; >50% offline eval; human review most popular

takeaways.what_they_do: 70% update prompts at least monthly and 10% daily, yet 31% have no way of managing prompts — implying versioned prompt storage is a real gap teams hit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a full 31% of respondents don't have any way of managing their prompts

takeaways.what_they_do: Most production agents have write access, typically with a human in the loop, and some act independently; the speaker flags permissioning as an open area.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the majority of agents already in production do have right access uh typically with a human in the loop

takeaways.technique: Expect frequent model churn; keep routing abstracted
takeaways.what_they_do: Over 50% of teams swap models at least monthly and 17% weekly, so integration churn is normal and routing should be decoupled from call sites.
takeaways.evidence_quote: more than 50% are updating their models at least monthly, 17% weekly
